events.text: A summer storm stands over the pool where you were an egg, a thousand years and more ago. You have flown through a hundred storms since you grew wings. This one is different: for the first time, the thunder does not sound like heaven's lightning sent against you. It sounds like a question.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Coil in the heart of the storm, and listen

effects.log: The bolts walk around you like monks around a pagoda. Between two of them you hear it: thunder is the sky clearing its throat before it speaks.

choices.text: Swallow a bolt, as you did when you were young

effects.log: It goes down hot and bright, as it always did. It makes you stronger. It does not make you understand it.

choices.text: Climb above the storm, where it cannot reach

effects.log: Above the cloud the sky is still and blue, and you are safe, as you have been for centuries. Below, the thunder goes on asking someone else.

events.text: In the long quiet after the storm you remember every change that failed: the hatchling thrown back into the shallows, the river serpent knocked flat in the reeds, the cloud-seeker falling out of the sky with its claw empty. Each time, a bolt found you halfway out of the old body.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Let the old anger at heaven rise

effects.log: The reverse scale burns under your chin. For a week the wells of a valley run dry, and you feel strong and do not feel wiser.

choices.text: Remember each fall, one by one

effects.log: You count them, all the way down. Each time the bolt came, it came exactly where you were weakest. It was not punishing. It was pointing.

choices.text: Forgive heaven for them

effects.log: You forgive the sky. It is kind of you, and the sky does not seem to notice.

events.text: Two village children come out into the rain by the old pool and look up at you in the cloud. One of them shouts "A dragon!" and the other, at the same moment, "A snake!" The old word goes through you like a nail, as it once did, and then it does not.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Show yourself whole, so there can be no doubt

effects.log: You come down out of the cloud, horns and wings and all. Both children shout "Dragon!" now, and run home to tell it. Nobody has learned anything, including you.

choices.text: Let them both be right

effects.log: The thunder answers you both the same. A sound means nothing until someone hears it, and each of them hears their own. Thunder is not the bolt. It is the hearing.

choices.text: Hide in the cloud, as the old fear tells you

effects.log: You go up into the grey and wait until they go in. The fear is very old, and it fits you like a skin you forgot to shed.

events.text: It is the day of the Awakening of Insects, when the first thunder of spring is supposed to wake the frogs and the beetles in the cold mud. Nobody has made it yet this year. The paddies wait, silent.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Make the first thunder of spring, and nothing more

effects.log: One long roll over the valley, no bolt at all. In every paddy at once the frogs wake and begin to argue. Thunder was never a weapon. It is how the world is told to wake.

choices.text: Make it loud, so heaven knows who made it

effects.log: You shake every roof tile in the province. The frogs wake, and so do the exorcists, and the story of the year is about you.

choices.text: Let spring come without you this year

effects.log: You stay silent. The frogs wake anyway, a few days late, grumbling. The thunder serves; it was never the thunder's spring.

events.text: In the next storm another shape is in the cloud: a long dry dragon with cracked scales and eyes like a kiln, the Drought Dragon you would have become if the woodcutter's word had been the last one. It offers you its spite. "It is thunder too," it says.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Speak to it as your own other face

ok.log: You speak, and it listens, because it is you. Spite is thunder that never learned to stop. You take it back into yourself, and it goes quiet, and the rain comes behind it.

fail.log: You speak, and it laughs your own laugh back at you and rakes you across the flank before it goes. Something was true in what you said, all the same.

choices.text: Drive it out of the sky with lightning

effects.log: You win. It goes, smoking, to the south, and a dry wind follows it. You have beaten it; you have not understood it.

choices.text: Let it go its own way

effects.log: It goes. You watch it out of sight, and are sorry for it, which is a beginning.

events.text: The storm gathers over the pool where you hatched, the whole sky leaning in. It is not coming for you. It is waiting for you, the way a word waits for the mouth that says it. You understand the thunder now. If you let go of the dragon, you will be it.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You fly down through the rain to the old pool, and coil there a while longer, a dragon among frogs. The storm will wait. Storms are patient, it turns out.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Thunder

effects.log: You stop holding the shape of a dragon. The storm takes the rest.

events.text: The thunder speaks, and you almost understand it. Almost is a long way from the Dao. Something in the steps you took was a step aside, and the sky knows it.
events.arc: The Imugi: The Dao of Thunder

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: You lie in the storm for ten more years, letting the thunder go over and over you, until you can hear the parts of it you missed.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be a dragon, and that is not small. The rains still come when you call them.

events.text: Thunder out of a clear sky, three times, over the jade pavilions. The immortals look up. Something enormous and winged comes down through the cloud, and the rain comes with it, and it lands in front of you and looks at you as if it had been looking for a thousand years. "You were me," it says, in a voice like a storm a long way off. "I waited in a pool for you to come up here."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow to it. It touches its brow to yours, very lightly, and goes back up into the storm, and the storm goes with it.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Thunder from it

effects.log: It opens its jaws, and the thunder that comes out is a word, and you understand the word.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks at your world below, small and blue, and nods its great head once. "Someone has to make its first thunder," it says.

events.text: A child's kite from your valley breaks its string at the spring festival and goes east, over your ridge, on the warm wind. You follow it out of old habit. Somewhere over the third valley you notice that the wind does not belong to you. You belong to it.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Call the wind back to your valley

effects.log: It comes, as it always has, obedient as a dog. The kite falls into your own river. You fish it out for the child. The wind waits to be let go.

choices.text: Follow the kite wherever the wind goes

effects.log: It lands at last in a stranger's paddy three valleys over, where a stranger's child picks it up and laughs. The wind did not care whose valley it was. That is what made it the wind.

choices.text: Ride the wind, but keep one eye on the Ward

effects.log: You go with it half the way and come home before dark, as a good guardian does, having learned half of something.

events.text: Harvest. The farmers of your valley toss the threshed rice up in winnowing baskets, and the wind takes the chaff and leaves the grain. You lit the Winnowing Basket star a long time ago. You thought you knew what judgement was.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Watch what the wind takes, and what it leaves

effects.log: The wind does not judge. It lifts what is light. The grain stays because it is heavy with itself. You have been winnowing your valley for centuries, and never once like this.

choices.text: Blow for them yourself, to make the work go faster

effects.log: The chaff flies off in a golden cloud, and the farmers cheer, and are done by noon. You have been useful. You have not been the wind.

choices.text: Judge the valley's houses, as the star taught you

effects.log: You weigh each house and bless the honest ones. It is good, careful work. It is the work of a dragon who owns a valley.

events.text: You lie as the left ridge of your valley, as you have for centuries, and the wind cannot pass through a ridge. It goes around. To be the wind you would have to stop being a ridge, if only for a season, and the Ward has never once been without you.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Stay as you are: the Ward needs its ridge

effects.log: The valley sleeps sheltered behind you, as it always has. The wind goes round, as it always has.

choices.text: Breathe, and let a little wind through your pines

effects.log: A draught moves through the valley for the first time in living memory. The old pines creak. It is a little, and it is not nothing.

choices.text: Lift from the ridge for one season

effects.log: For a season the valley lies open to the east. The pines lean, the smoke of every kitchen goes the same way, and nobody comes to harm. In autumn the air in the valley is new.

events.text: The White Tiger on the right ridge watches you with yellow eyes. "The wind you want to be," it says, "will blow on my ridge too. And on the hunters' camp. And on the Fire Mountain. Have you thought about that, little brother?"
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: "Then it will blow on yours as gently as on mine"

effects.log: The tiger is quiet for a long time. Then it lies down with its back to the wind, the way it would lie down beside a friend.

choices.text: "The east is mine. The wind will know its side"

effects.log: The tiger laughs, which tigers seldom do. "Then you will never be wind," it says, and turns away.

choices.text: Say nothing, and send a warm wind over the tiger's ridge

effects.log: The tiger closes its eyes in the warm air. It does not thank you. It does not have to.

events.text: The villagers raise a new shrine at the head of the valley. Over the door they have carved: "The Azure Dragon Makes the Spring." They burn incense there every morning, and the smoke goes up into your nostrils, sweet and heavy, like pride.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Accept the shrine: the spring is yours, after all

effects.log: You let the smoke go to your head. It is very pleasant. That spring the wind is a little heavier than it should be.

choices.text: Blow out the incense, gently, every morning

effects.log: The priest relights it, and you blow it out, every morning for a year, until he gives up and plants a willow by the door instead. The wind plays in its branches. It is better.

choices.text: Teach the priest what the wind has taught you

ok.log: You come to the priest in a dream and say one thing: the wind owns nothing. In the morning he chisels the board smooth and carves a new line: "The Spring Comes."

fail.log: You come to the priest in a dream, and he wakes sure that the dragon wants a bigger shrine. You have a lot to learn about speaking.

events.text: The first warm wind of the year is gathering out over the eastern sea, the one that has blown over your valley every spring since you were an egg in a well. You know it now, all of it: what it lifts, what it leaves, how it owns nothing and touches everything. If you let go of the dragon, you will be it.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You lie down along your ridge for one more spring, and let the wind go over you, and the valley does not know how close it came to losing its dragon.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Wind

effects.log: You open your claws on the valley, on the stars, on the name. The wind takes what is light.

events.text: You reach for the wind and it slips through your claws, as it should, and you are still holding on to something. The valley, the stars, the name: something in you has not been winnowed yet.
events.arc: The Azure Dragon: The Dao of Wind

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more springs on the ridge, letting the wind go over you, until you can feel which part of you it cannot lift.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the dragon of the east, and the valley will have its ridge. The wind will forgive you.

events.text: A warm wind comes across the jade terraces out of nowhere, smelling of wet paddies and pine, and all the immortals' sleeves lift at once. In the middle of it, as if the wind had decided to have a shape, there is an azure dragon. It circles you once. "There you are," it says. "You were an egg in a well, and then you were me."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow. It goes round you once more, lifting your hair, and then it is only a wind again, going east.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Wind from it

effects.log: It breathes out, and the wind goes into you, and for a moment you own nothing at all, and it is wonderful.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down through the clouds at your world. "A world needs a spring wind," it says. "Every year. I can do that."

events.text: A swordsman climbs to your shrine on the pass with a sword across both palms. In one night, he says, it cut down a tyrant and an innocent stable boy, and he does not know if it is a good sword or a cursed one. He asks the Autumn Court to judge the sword.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Judge the swordsman, not the sword

effects.log: You judge him, fairly, and send him down the mountain to the boy's mother. It is a good verdict. It is the court's work, not the sword's.

choices.text: Look at the edge for a whole night

effects.log: An edge has no mercy and no severity. It goes where it is sent, and the sending is the whole of justice. By dawn you understand why the old tigers had no swords: they were swords.

choices.text: Break the sword between your teeth

effects.log: It snaps like a reed. The swordsman weeps with relief. The question goes on living, unbroken.

events.text: The beam of the Autumn Court tilts again this season: too many pardons last year, so now the hand reaches for severity, to even it. The magpie on the eaves clicks its tongue. You have been doing this for centuries: a pardon here, a punishment there, to keep the beam level.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Pardon, to balance last year's punishments

effects.log: The beam evens. You have balanced the court, and not cut a single case cleanly.

choices.text: Let the magpie decide this season

effects.log: The magpie decides. It is no worse a judge than most, and you rest.

choices.text: Stop weighing. Cut each case once, exactly

effects.log: Each verdict comes out of you like a claw out of its sheath: once, all the way, and back. The beam does not tilt. A cut that leans is a cut that misses.

events.text: The ghosts you made when you were young and hungry still walk the pass ahead of you some nights, calling names in the voices of mothers. A blade that does not clean itself rusts. You have always known that about blades.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Let them walk: they are your record

effects.log: They walk on before you, calling. The travellers fear the pass, and the pass is safe, and nothing in you is clean.

choices.text: Lay the last of them to rest yourself

effects.log: One by one you lead them down to their villages, to cairns and turned-over pots and kitchens where somebody still sets out a bowl. The last one thanks you. You are a lighter blade.

choices.text: Ask the mountain god to take them

effects.log: The old man takes them with a sigh, and a look that says this was your work to do.

events.text: Autumn's first frost is due on the grass. It kills the weak stalks and leaves the strong; the farmers need it to sweeten the persimmons and to break the pests. It is the oldest cut in the world, and you are the tiger who breathes it out.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Hold the frost back so the late beans can come in

effects.log: You hold your breath a week. The beans come in, and the pests with them. Mercy is not the same as kindness.

choices.text: Breathe it a week early, to be sure

effects.log: Frost on the beans and frost on the pests. It is just, and it is too much. A sword drawn too soon is a sword that has not been looked at.

choices.text: Breathe it exactly on its day

effects.log: The frost comes on its night, white and quiet and precise, and the morning is clean, and nothing is cut that did not have to be. You feel the edge of the world go straight.

events.text: The Azure Dragon of the left ridge comes to you at the turning of the year. "They say you are looking for the sword," it says. "Show me." It is not an insult. It is the oldest kind of courtesy between the two ridges.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Fight it with one stroke only

ok.log: You stand still until the very end of waiting, and cut once. The dragon looks at the line of frost along its scales and bows. "That was not mercy and it was not severity," it says. "That was the sword."

fail.log: You cut once, and it is not clean, and the dragon's tail knocks you the length of the ridge. "Close," it says, kindly.

choices.text: Refuse: a sword drawn to show itself is no sword

effects.log: The dragon thinks about it, and nods. "Then you are nearer than I am," it says.

choices.text: Fight it all day, claw and roar

effects.log: You fight from dawn to dusk, and the valley between the ridges thunders, and you are both very pleased with yourselves. Nothing is cut that matters.

events.text: It is the first night of autumn, and the beam of the Autumn Court is level, and you are not holding it level. Every verdict you ever gave, the merciful and the severe, was one motion trying to be found. You have found it. If you let go of the tiger, you will be it.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You go back up to the pass and sit above the road at dusk, as you always have, and keep the blade sheathed one more autumn.

choices.text: Become the Sword Dao

effects.log: You let the stripes go, and the court, and the mountain. What is left is an edge.

events.text: You reach for the sword in yourself and find a scale instead, still swinging. Somewhere in the long road you leaned, and the edge remembers it.
events.arc: The White Tiger: The Sword Dao

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more autumns at the court, cutting once and watching where the cut goes, until you can find the place you leaned.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the White Tiger of the west, and the court will have its judge. It is a just life.

events.text: The first frost of the Upper Realm comes in one night, white and precise on every jade roof, and in the morning there are tiger tracks in it leading to your door, and a white tiger sitting at the end of them as still as a drawn blade. "I was the tiger," it says. "You were the tiger. Now I am the edge, and you have come all this way. Sit."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You sit with it until the frost melts. When you look up, it has gone, and there is one clean cut in the morning air.

choices.text: Take the Sword Dao from it

effects.log: It looks at you, once, and you understand a cut that is neither mercy nor severity, and you will never forget it.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world below. "Every world needs one cut it can trust," it says. "Its autumn. I will keep it."

events.text: Deep winter. The two heads argue under the river ice, as they have for a thousand years: the snake says the river is still, frozen through, the tortoise says it is moving. You have never once settled it. The ice is very thick this year.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: The snake is right: break the ice and look

effects.log: The snake strikes the ice, and it cracks, and the cold rushes in. The river is moving. The snake is annoyed, and you are frozen for a month.

choices.text: The tortoise is right: wait for spring and see

effects.log: You wait. In spring the ice goes out, and the river was moving all along. The tortoise is pleased. The snake sulks.

choices.text: Let the tortoise listen and the snake look, together

effects.log: The tortoise hears it and the snake sees it, at the same moment: it moves. Under the ice, in the dark, it never once stopped. Waiting is a kind of going.

events.text: In a cave behind a waterfall a drop of water falls on a stone, once a breath, as it has since before there were tortoises. There is a hollow in the stone the size of your head. The snake wants to count the drops. The tortoise wants to sit.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Watch a thousand years of drops

effects.log: You watch until the hollow is a little deeper. Patience has a shape, and it is the shape water makes in stone. Cunning has a shape too. It is the same one.

choices.text: Let the snake count, and say how long the stone has left

effects.log: The snake counts all year and says: eleven thousand years. It is pleased to know. Knowing is not the same as seeing.

choices.text: Move the stone out from under the drip

effects.log: You shove the stone aside with your shell, kindly. The drop falls on bare rock and begins again. It does not mind at all.

events.text: You turn your shell to the light and look at the thirteen plates, all the endings you witnessed, written true. One plate the snake wrote without seeing, long ago, is cracked. Still water shows a thing as it is. You have never once looked at your own back.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Write the plate over once more, carefully

effects.log: You write it again, and better. It will hold. You are a good record-keeper.

choices.text: Leave the shell as it is: a record is a record

effects.log: You let the crack be. It was true that you wrote it badly. That is also a record.

choices.text: Lay the shell in still water, and read it in the reflection

effects.log: In the still pool your back is a night sky, every plate a star, and the cracked one only a star seen through a ripple. Water does not lie. It does not judge, either.

events.text: The Dragon King of the East Sea sends for his oldest envoy. He wants a river dammed, to make a lake for a new palace under the water, and he wants the tortoise who holds the winter to hold this river still.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Dam it as asked

effects.log: You hold the river, and the lake fills, and the palace is very beautiful. Downstream the mills stop. The king is pleased with you.

choices.text: Refuse: water that is held breaks out somewhere else

effects.log: The Dragon King is cold to you for a century. In the spring floods, three other rivers that were dammed break their banks, and yours does not, because it is still running.

choices.text: Dam it, but leave a way for the fish

effects.log: The lake fills, and the fish go round it by a side stream, and the mills turn slowly. It is a good half answer.

events.text: One night the snake says, very quietly: "If we are one water, we do not need the knot." It has been wanting to uncoil for a thousand years, and you have been afraid of it for a thousand years. Now it is not asking to leave. It is asking you to trust it.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Then let go of the knot, and see if you stay

ok.log: You loosen the last coil. Nothing holds the two of you together, and you stay together, and the snake laughs, which it has never done. That was always the knot: the staying, not the rope.

fail.log: You loosen the coil, and the snake slides a hand's width away before it comes back, frightened. Not yet. But it came back.

choices.text: Talk it through over a game of stones

effects.log: You play stones on the riverbed all night. The snake wins. You are closer than before, and still tied.

choices.text: Tighten the knot: you will not lose it

effects.log: You pull the coil tight. The snake goes quiet, and the knot holds, and the question goes under the ice for another century.

events.text: The river under the ice is moving, and you can feel all of it: every drop that has worn a stone, every flood that found its way, every winter that waited. The tortoise and the snake have stopped being two. If you let go of the shell, you will be the water.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You settle into the black sand of the riverbed one more winter, both heads under the ice, and listen to the water going on.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Water

effects.log: The two heads turn and face each other, for the last time, and see the same thing.

events.text: You try to be the water, and the two heads go two ways, as they have always gone. Something between them is still a knot, not a river.
events.arc: The Black Tortoise: The Dao of Water

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more winters under the ice, the heads talking, until you find where they still pull apart.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Black Tortoise of the north, two heads and one shell, keeping the record. It is enough.

events.text: All the fountains of the jade city stop at once, and the water in them stands up, and something old and black and patient walks out of the largest pool: a tortoise with a snake around it, its two heads turned to face each other, and both of them turn to face you. "We have been waiting," says the snake. "We are good at it," says the tortoise.
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow to both heads. They bow back, one slow, one quick, and walk into the pool, and the fountains run again.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Water from it

effects.log: The two heads speak together, one word, and the word is water, and it runs into you and finds its way.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: The snake looks down at your world, and the tortoise nods. "Its rivers will run true," they say together. "We will see to it."

events.text: Two farmers drag a boundary stone into your courtyard and argue over it. You lower your horn to find the liar, as you have ten thousand times. The horn points at neither of them. Both are partly right, and both are partly lying, and the horn does not know what to do.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Butt the one who is more wrong

effects.log: You butt him gently. The other farmer goes home pleased, and the stone stands where he wanted it, and next year they will both be back.

choices.text: Lie down between them until they move the stone themselves

effects.log: They argue all afternoon over your back. By dusk the stone sits where both of them can live with it. The horn never moved. The scale did.

choices.text: Tell each of them what the other is hiding

effects.log: They are both very ashamed, and settle it, and avoid you for a year. Clarity is a kind of balance. It is not all of it.

events.text: For centuries you have eaten only the bitter leaf, to keep the horn clean. Today a child holds up a ripe persimmon to you over the courtyard wall, sweet and soft, because the child thinks you look hungry.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Refuse it, kindly

effects.log: You lower your head to thank the child, and do not eat. The horn stays very clean, and very narrow.

choices.text: Eat the persimmon, and then a bitter leaf

effects.log: Sweet, then bitter. The mouth is not cleaner for only bitterness; it is truer for knowing both. The child is delighted.

choices.text: Eat it, and forget the bitter leaf this year

effects.log: It is delicious. You eat persimmons all autumn, and the horn grows cloudy, and you are happy, and a little lost.

events.text: From the palace gate you watch the Fire Mountain, as you have for centuries, swallowing its sparks before they reach the city's dry lies. Tonight, for the first time, you wonder what the mountain is for. Fire faces you. You face fire. Neither of you has ever moved.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Sit with the mountain, and feel what it balances

effects.log: Without the Fire Mountain the city would be cold and wet and rotten, a city of mould. Without you it would burn. Neither of you is the enemy. You are the two pans of one scale.

choices.text: Swallow its spark, as you always have

effects.log: You swallow it. The city sleeps. You are a good guardian, and you have not asked the mountain anything.

choices.text: Ask the court to dig another pond against it

effects.log: The court digs a pond, and puts a stone fire-eater in it, and is reassured. The mountain does not notice.

events.text: An old widow lies before the magistrate to save her son from a cruel sentence, and your horn knows it at once, the way a tongue knows salt. The law says to lower your head at the liar. The magistrate is waiting for you to do it.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Look away, this once

effects.log: You look away. The son goes free, and you have lied with your eyes, and the horn will remember it.

choices.text: Lower your head at the widow, as the law says

effects.log: You lower your head. The son is sentenced. The law was kept, and the scale was not.

choices.text: Weigh the lie and the cruelty together

effects.log: You weigh them in the same pan, the widow's lie and the magistrate's cruelty, and the scale tips, and you turn and lower your head at the magistrate. Nobody in the courtyard breathes.

events.text: The Judge of Heaven sends for you: there are liars in the heavenly court too, and the seat at the foot of the judgement throne has been empty for an age. You go up. The judge is very old, and very tired, and very sure.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Refuse the seat

effects.log: You come back down to the palace gate. The horn is clean, and the judge is still sure, and heaven still has its liars.

choices.text: Weigh only the accused, as you were asked

effects.log: You sit a season at the judge's feet and find three liars. It is good work. The judge thanks you, and is sure of everything else.

choices.text: Weigh the judge himself

ok.log: You lower your horn, very slowly, at the throne. The court goes silent. The judge looks down at you for a long time, and then gets up and sits on the floor beside you, and the throne is empty, and the scale is level.

fail.log: You lower your horn at the throne, and the judge's guards drive you from the court with spears. You were not wrong. You were not ready.

events.text: Before the palace gate, facing the Fire Mountain, you understand at last that the horn never judged anyone. It only weighed, and the weighing was the law, and there is no hand on the scale, and never was. If you let go of the beast, you will be the balance.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You lie down before the gate one more year, facing the mountain, and the officials dismount before you, as they always have.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Balance

effects.log: You lower your horn, at nobody, for the last time.

events.text: You try to be the balance, and the horn moves on its own toward someone. It is still pointing. Somewhere along the way you went on judging.
events.arc: The Haechi: The Dao of Balance

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years at the gate, weighing and not pointing, until the horn learns to be still.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Haechi before the gate, and the horn will see true. A city needs that too.

events.text: In the hall of the jade court two immortals are quarrelling over a peach tree, loudly, and all at once neither of them can say a word. A beast like a horned ram is standing between them, clean-white, a little bell at its throat, and it is looking at you. "I used to point," it says. "You know. You were there. Now I only weigh."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow to it, and it bows back, and the bell rings once, and the quarrel over the peach tree is settled in a breath.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Balance from it

effects.log: It touches its horn to your brow, very lightly, and for a moment you can feel the weight of everything, and none of it tips.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down through the cloud at your world. "Every quarrel there could be weighed honestly," it says. "I would like that."

events.text: The bamboo flowers across the whole mountain, once in sixty years, a white haze over the green. You know what comes after: the stalks die, the rats come for the seed, the lean years. You have lived through it many times. You have never once watched it to the end.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Gather seed for the lean years

effects.log: You fill every hollow on the ridge with seed. You will not go hungry. You flew past the end of the story again.

choices.text: Sing over the flowering

effects.log: You sing, and the mountain is beautiful, and the song is about the flowers. It is not yet about what comes after them.

choices.text: Watch one stand of bamboo flower and die, to the very end

effects.log: It flowers, and drops its seed, and goes brown and dry and falls. And under the dead stalks, by the first frost, there are seedlings the height of your claw.

events.text: At dawn you call from the high ridge, as you always have. Below, in a plain nest in a plain pine, a sparrow chick calls too, thin and loud. Its parent answers it from the next branch. It is not your call and not your answer, and you cannot stop listening.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Listen to the answer, not the call

effects.log: The call is not life. Life is that something answers. You have been calling for ten thousand mornings and listening for half of them.

choices.text: Answer the chick too

effects.log: You call back. The chick is astonished into silence, and its parent is very cross with you.

choices.text: Fly on: plain birds are not your concern

effects.log: You fly on to the paulownia slope and sing to the sunrise, beautifully, alone.

events.text: A war has burned the paulownia slope where you sang for three hundred years. One tree stands, black to the top, dead as charcoal. You rest only on the paulownia. You have never once rested on a dead one.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Find another paulownia

effects.log: You find a young one in a valley to the south and settle on it. The burned slope is behind you.

choices.text: Plant a paulownia seed in the ashes

effects.log: You scratch a seed into the ash with your claw. It will grow, or not. It is a kindness.

choices.text: Rest on the burned tree anyway

effects.log: You settle on the black branch, and it holds you. In spring a green shoot comes up from the stump, an arm's length from your feet. The tree was dead. The tree was not done.

events.text: A ruler you once came to in the dance, long ago, a good one, lies dying in a cold hall. He has sent for you. "You are the sign of heaven's favour," he says. "Ask heaven to let me live."
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Dance for him one last time

effects.log: You dance in the cold hall, and he weeps, and dies happy, and the court says he died with heaven's favour. It is a beautiful death. It is not what he asked.

choices.text: Bring him water from a sweet spring

effects.log: He drinks, and lives a month longer, and is grateful for the month.

choices.text: Refuse, gently, and stay with him to the end

effects.log: "Life is not the thing that does not end," you tell him. "It is the thing that goes on." You stay until his breath stops, and then you sing, and outside a child is born in the palace kitchen.

events.text: Rats have come for the bamboo seed after the flowering, as they always do: a pair of them, then a hundred, then the whole ridge alive with them, eating the seed you would have eaten. They are the famine animal. They are life too, hungrier than you.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Drive them off the ridge

effects.log: You drive them down the mountain in a rush of wings. The seed is yours. The rats go to the villages, which is worse for everyone.

choices.text: Let them eat

effects.log: You fold your wings and let them eat. They have more young than you will ever have. Life does not ask you whether it may go on.

choices.text: Sing until the owls come, and only enough of them

ok.log: You sing all night, and the owls come down out of the dark, a few, enough. By morning there are rats and seed and owls, and the mountain is in balance, and every one of them alive.

fail.log: You sing, and the owls come, too many, and the ridge is quiet and full of feathers by dawn. You meant well. Life is not a song.

events.text: The bamboo is flowering again on the far mountain, white against the green, and you are not afraid of what comes after it. Life is not the bird that appears in peace. It is the reason anything goes on at all, and you can feel the reason, under your feathers. If you let go of the bird, you will be it.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You fly to the paulownia slope and sing one more dawn, and something, somewhere, answers.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Life

effects.log: You open your wings over the flowering mountain, and do not close them again.

events.text: You try to be life, and you are still a bird looking at it, very beautifully, from a branch. Something in you is still waiting to be answered.
events.arc: The Phoenix: The Dao of Life

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years on the high ridge, calling and listening, until you know what you are still waiting for.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Phoenix, seen only in peace. Peace is not a small thing to be.

events.text: Every tree on the jade terraces flowers at once, out of season, and every bird in the Upper Realm starts singing. Down through the blossom comes a bird of five colours, as big as a hall, and it settles on the branch beside you, and the branch holds it. "I was the Phoenix," it says. "And you were. Something answered me, at the end. I came to answer you."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow, and it sings one note, and in the gardens below a thousand seeds that were never going to sprout put up green shoots.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Life from it

effects.log: It sings, and the song goes into your chest and stays, warm, like a second heart beating a little behind your own.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world, small and green. "Things should grow there," it says. "I will see that they do."

events.text: The first sage you ever heralded died long ago, and you saw them home. Today you pass their grave and find a boy you have never seen, pulling weeds and planting grass, carefully, so as not to bend any of it. The ribbon you tied came home a century ago. Something is still knotting.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Bow at the grave, and go on

effects.log: You bow. The boy does not see you. You walk on lightly, and the grass you walk on does not bend.

choices.text: Ask the boy who taught him to plant like that

effects.log: His teacher's teacher's teacher was the sage. The ribbon you tied went on knotting itself long after you let go. Nothing sown is ever quite finished.

choices.text: Walk on: that ribbon came home already

effects.log: You walk on. It is true. It is not the whole truth.

events.text: In the forest a blade of grass bends under your hoof, by accident, for the first time in sixty years. The Unbent Grass, broken. You stop, and look down, and for once you do not look at the count. You look at the grass.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Straighten it with your breath

effects.log: You breathe on it, and it stands. You have mended a harm. You have not seen where it went.

choices.text: Watch where the harm goes

effects.log: The beetle under the blade moves house. The house it moves to was a thrush's supper. The thrush goes hungry and sings less, and a fox sleeps late. A harm is a stone in a pond. So is a kindness.

choices.text: Go on lightly, as you always have

effects.log: You go on, lighter than before, careful of every step. The count begins again.

events.text: At the mouth of the Qilin Cave an old hunter lies starving: the hunter who broke your foreleg in a bad age, centuries ago, when you would not strike back. He does not know you. He has no strength left to hunt anything.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Let the mountain decide

effects.log: You step around him into the cave. The mountain decides, as mountains do. In the morning he is gone.

choices.text: Show him where the chestnuts fall

effects.log: You walk ahead of him, slowly, to the chestnut grove, and he follows and eats, and lives.

choices.text: Feed him with your own hand, and stay until he is well

effects.log: You stay all winter. He never knows you. In spring he goes down the mountain and never hunts again, and teaches his grandchildren to leave the deer at the spring alone. What was sown came home.

events.text: Two armies face each other across a river valley, and you could walk between them; you have done it before, and they stopped. But the last war you stopped started again in ten years. You have never once asked why.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Walk between them, as you always have

effects.log: They stop, and throw down their spears, and go home. In twelve years they are back.

choices.text: Walk to the cause instead

effects.log: You walk past both camps to the two kings' quarrel, and through it to an older one, and to the first stone thrown, eighty years ago, over a well. You stand at the well until both kings come to see why. It is the first time either of them has looked at it.

choices.text: Stand on the field until they leave

effects.log: You stand in the long grass between them. A spear is thrown, and another, and you do not move. At dusk they go home, ashamed, and you are hurt.

events.text: The jade book lies open under your hoof. You can spit it for a newborn: the words of what a person could be. You have done it for sages. Tonight it is for a weaver's baby in a hut, and you understand, as you open your mouth, that every word you write is a cause.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Write the child kindly, as you always have

effects.log: You write a good life. The baby sleeps. Somewhere a wheel begins to turn that the child did not choose.

choices.text: Leave the page blank for the child to write

effects.log: You leave it blank, and the baby takes the brush in its fist and makes a mark. It is not a word. It is the child's own. You have never given a greater gift.

choices.text: Read your own page first

ok.log: You read your own page, and it is all ribbons, tied and brought home and tied again, and you understand that you were never the one who tied them. You were the road.

fail.log: You read your own page, and cannot make it out, and your horn aches for a month.

events.text: It is a good age, and you stand on the Morning-Heaven Stone where the old qilin-horse went up, and you can see every ribbon at once: every cause you tied, every return you brought home, threads going out through the world and back. Nothing harmed is ever quite gone. Nothing given is either. If you let go of the qilin, you will be it.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You walk down off the stone and into the forest, lightly, and the grass does not bend, and one more ribbon waits.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Karma

effects.log: You step off the Morning-Heaven Stone, and do not come down.

events.text: You try to be the road the ribbons travel, and you are still counting them. Somewhere a ribbon you tied did not come home, and you have not yet followed it.
events.arc: The Qilin: The Dao of Karma

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years in the forest, following the threads out and back, until you find the one you lost.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Qilin, the sign of a good age. A good age is a great deal.

events.text: A deer steps out of the clouds onto the jade road, and it is not a deer: dragon scales on its back, a horn tipped with soft flesh, five colours in its coat, and pale flame round its hooves that burns nothing. Where it walks the moss on the stones stands up. It stops in front of you. "You were me," it says, in a voice like a temple bell. "I followed a ribbon here."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow. It touches your sleeve with its soft horn, and walks away into the cloud, and the moss stays standing.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Karma from it

effects.log: It speaks one word, and you can feel every cause you ever set going, out in the world, coming home to you.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down through the cloud at your world. "Every kindness there should find its way back," it says. "I can walk that road."

events.text: A thirsty child at a village well tries to scoop the moon out of the bucket with both hands, laughing, and spills it every time. You have worn faces for thousands of years. You sit on the well wall in the shape of a cat and watch.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Show the child the real moon

effects.log: You point with your chin at the sky. The child looks up, and then back down at the bucket, disappointed. The real one is too far.

choices.text: Let the child believe the moon is caught

effects.log: The child carries the bucket home very carefully, and shows the moon to a grandmother. Both are happy. You are not sure what you have done.

choices.text: Look at the moon in the bucket for a long time

effects.log: It is not the moon. It is not a lie, either: it is the moon, held. Every illusion you ever made was a true thing held in a strange cup.

events.text: In a dream, every face you ever wore sits down in a row in front of you: the widow, the scholar, the wine-seller, the aunt, the monk, and the others, hundreds of them, waiting. Not one of them was you. Every one of them was.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Burn the faces

effects.log: You burn them one by one. It is a relief. When you wake you have no faces left, and a cold nose.

choices.text: Put on the kindest one again

effects.log: You put on the widow, who was kind, and walk in her a while. It is like coming home to a house you rented.

choices.text: Speak to each face, and ask what it saw

effects.log: Each one tells you what it saw, and none of them saw the same world. All of them were true while they were worn. That was never the lie. The lie was thinking there was a face underneath.

events.text: On the hill road a salt peddler stops dead and stares at you, as salt peddlers do, and you feel your tails show behind you in the evening light. For a thousand years you would have run. Tonight you do not, and neither does he.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Ask him what he sees

effects.log: "A fox," he says, slowly. "And a person. I am not sure which one is the trick." Neither are you. That is the first honest thing anyone has said to you in an age.

choices.text: Run, as foxes do

effects.log: You run, all nine tails, up into the pines. He tells the story at every inn on the road.

choices.text: Show him a face so good he doubts his salt

effects.log: He rubs his eyes, and sniffs his salt, and goes on, muttering. You are very good. You are still running, in a way.

events.text: A child in a farmhouse wakes screaming every night from the same dream: the dark under the bed. You could give the child a mask to dream in, the face of a brave general, and the dark would be only dark.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Give the child the general's face to dream in

effects.log: The child dreams as a general and marches into the dark under the bed with a paper sword, and the dark is only dark. The mask was false. The courage was not.

choices.text: Swallow the fear into your bead

effects.log: You take the fear into your bead, and the child sleeps. The fear is yours now. It is quite heavy.

choices.text: Leave it: dreams are not your trade

effects.log: You go on up the hill. The child goes on screaming, until one night they stop.

events.text: A young scholar on your hill road has worked out what you are and wants your bead, not to steal: to learn. "Give it to me," the scholar says, "and tell me to look at the sky." You know that story. You know how it ends.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Give the scholar a false bead that teaches as well as the true one

ok.log: You make a bead out of a river pebble and a little moonlight, and it teaches the scholar everything the real one would have. It was never the bead. It was the looking.

fail.log: You make a false bead, and the scholar sees through it at once and goes away hurt. You will have to be truer than that.

choices.text: Give nothing, and walk the road with the scholar a while

effects.log: You walk together to the next village, talking. The scholar learns a little, and so do you.

choices.text: Keep the bead in your mouth, and run

effects.log: You run, and keep the bead, and the scholar shouts after you. It is safe. You are safe.

events.text: On a full-moon night you sit on the grave mound where you were born, and in every cup of water in the valley there is a moon, and every one of them is true. You understand the masks at last: they were never lies. The world wears faces too, and you can see through all of them to the moon. If you let go of the fox, you will be it.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You put on one more face, an old woman's, and go down to the village for one more night of tea and stories.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Illusion

effects.log: You take off the last face, and there is nothing under it but the moon.

events.text: You reach for the Dao, and your hand turns into a paw, and the paw into a hand: you are still changing faces to reach it. Somewhere one face is still hiding from you.
events.arc: The Nine-Tailed Fox: The Dao of Illusion

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years on the grave mound under the moon, until you find the face you are hiding behind.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Nine-Tailed Fox of the mountain, and the moon will know you. It is a lovely life.

events.text: At a banquet of the immortals you look into your cup of wine and there is a moon in it, though it is noon. When you look up, the immortal across the table has nine tails, moon-coloured, folded neatly over the cushion. "You were me," it says, with your own smile. "I wore so many faces. This one I kept for you."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You raise your cup to it. It raises its own, and drinks the moon, and is only an empty cushion, and the cup is warm.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Illusion from it

effects.log: It looks at you, and for one breath you can see every face the world is wearing, and the moon under all of them.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world below. "Children there have bad dreams," it says. "Let me give them better faces to dream in."

events.text: You fly back to the house where you were born, a spark in a fire jar on the coldest night, nine generations of fire ago. The fire is still in the jar. A grandchild of a grandchild keeps it now, and does not know who you are, and puts a pine stick on it before bed.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Take a coal of it with you

effects.log: You take one coal, as a keepsake. It burns your claw a little all the way home. Kept fire does.

choices.text: Renew it with your own fire

effects.log: You breathe on it, and it leaps up new, and the house is warm all winter. You are a good giver of fire.

choices.text: Sit in its coals one night, and remember being a spark

effects.log: You sit in the jar until dawn, small as you were, and remember: you were never the fire. You were what the fire was given to. You were kept warm before you ever warmed anything.

events.text: One of your seven fires has turned fierce. Its keeper, a hard old headman, uses it to burn a rival's granary, and the swallows bring you the smoke. You have always called a misused fire home. It is what you do.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Call the fire home, as you always have

effects.log: You take it back, and the headman curses you, and the granaries are safe, and a village is colder this winter.

choices.text: Let it burn: it is theirs now

effects.log: You let it burn. It runs wild in the spring, as fierce fires do, and you are sorry.

choices.text: Go to the keeper, not the fire

effects.log: You perch on the headman's ridge-pole all winter, and talk with him, and warm him. In spring his fire is only a fire. A fire runs wild in a cold heart. It is the heart that wanted warming.

events.text: The swallows tell you of a high village with no fire at all, a whole winter of it: the last keeper died without an heir. Children there sleep in the cowshed for the warmth of the cows.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Stay the winter and keep the fire yourself

effects.log: You sit in their hearth all winter. They are warm, and grateful, and when you go in spring the hearth goes out behind you.

choices.text: Choose them a careful keeper

effects.log: You choose the shepherd's daughter, who is careful, and she keeps it, and it is a good fire.

choices.text: Give them a fire, and fly on without choosing a keeper

effects.log: You light the hearth and leave. They have to choose a keeper themselves, and argue, and choose, and the fire burns on. Fire given and trusted. You never even learn the keeper's name.

events.text: An envoy of the Southern Palace insults you before the other guardians: the youngest of the Four, a bird that plays with matches. You feel the old heat climb your throat. You know what you did the last time you swallowed a word like that.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Swallow it

effects.log: You swallow it, and it sits in you, smouldering, and you smile very politely all through the banquet.

choices.text: Answer him with fire, briefly

effects.log: One feather of flame, one word. He goes white and is careful with you for a hundred years. It was small. It was still fire kept for yourself.

choices.text: Sing it out into the sky as a red sunset

effects.log: You go out onto the terrace and sing it, all of it, and the whole southern sky goes red to the horizon. Fire that is given away does not burn the one who gives it.

events.text: There is one fire left that you have never given: the one in your own breast, that carries you over the sea and up to the sun. You have always known what giving it would mean. Tonight, for the first time, you think about it without being afraid.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Light a stranger's lamp with it, only a little

ok.log: You light a fisherman's lamp on the shore with one spark of your own fire, and it burns, and you are not smaller for it. You are warmer. That is the whole secret, and you have known it since you were a spark.

fail.log: You try to give a spark of yourself, and it tears coming out, and you lie on the shore a month, cold.

choices.text: Give a spark of it to the kitchen god of your first house

effects.log: You leave a spark under the kitchen god's shelf. The house will never be cold. It is a small giving, and a true one.

choices.text: Keep it: you need it to fly

effects.log: You keep it. You fly as high as ever. Kept fire burns, and it burns you a little, as it always has.

events.text: It is noon on the summer solstice, and you have crossed the sun, and every fire you ever gave is burning somewhere below you, none of them yours. Kept fire burns. Given fire warms. You understand it now all the way down, to the last fire, the one in your breast. If you give that one too, you will be it.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You fly down to the beacon hill and keep the watch one more summer, a bird of fire with a fire still in it.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Flame

effects.log: You open your breast to the world and give it the last fire.

events.text: You try to give the last fire, and your wings close around it by themselves. Somewhere you are still keeping something warm only for yourself.
events.arc: The Vermilion Bird: The Dao of Flame

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more summers on the swallow road, giving fires away, until you find the one you are still keeping.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Vermilion Bird of the south, and summer will come when you sing. That is a great deal of warmth.

events.text: Every lamp in the jade city lights at once at noon, and nobody lit them. A red bird comes down out of the sun onto the terrace in front of you, the size of a small hall, and the stones under it do not burn. "I was the bird," it says, and its voice is a hearth. "You were. I gave everything away, and look: I came to give you something too."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow, and it bows, and every lamp in the city goes out, and every cold room in the Upper Realm is warm all winter.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Flame from it

effects.log: It breathes on you, and the fire goes into you and does not burn, because you will give it away.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world. "Some hearth there is always cold," it says. "Not while I am there."

events.text: At a house-raising in a far village a child holds up a clod of yellow earth from the site, as the old custom says, and asks the ground to hold the house. You were a clod like that once, warm in a fist. You have never once been asked so simply.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Bless the house with luck

effects.log: The house is lucky for three generations. It is good work, a site spirit's work.

choices.text: Hold it, as you were asked

effects.log: You hold it. It is a light house, and you feel its weight on your back like a cat.

choices.text: Ask the ground what it holds

effects.log: You ask, and the ground tells you: every house that ever stood here, and every field and grave, and it has never felt any of them as weight. You have been carrying things the ground was only holding.

events.text: The Weight is heavy this year. A drought, a war on the border, a young king afraid of both: you can feel the capital settle a hair's breadth into you. You have always borne it. That is what the centre is for.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Bear it: you are the centre

effects.log: You bear it, all of it, and the capital stops sinking, and you are very tired.

choices.text: Hand a burden to the magistrate

effects.log: You give the magistrate the drought to manage, and he manages, badly, and the weight is less.

choices.text: Stop carrying, and lie under it

effects.log: Carrying is lifting against. Holding is lying beneath. You stop lifting, and lie still, and the capital rests on you as a house rests on a hill. The weight is the same. You are not.

events.text: The eighteen days before autumn: the year is handing itself over from summer, through you, as it does four times a year. You have always smoothed the hand-over, made it gentle, made it yours.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Be the hand-over, and nothing more

effects.log: Summer gives itself to autumn, and you do nothing at all but be the place where it happens. It is the smoothest hand-over in a thousand years. Earth does not do. Earth is where.

choices.text: Lengthen the hand-over for the harvest

effects.log: You hold summer back a week for the late rice. The harvest is good. Autumn is cross.

choices.text: Smooth it a little

effects.log: You ease it, a little, as you always have. It goes well.

events.text: A farming family buries its grandmother in the yellow clay above you, under a small mound, with rice wine and crying. You have held houses and palaces and pagodas. You have held the dead too, without ever thinking of it.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Turn the grave to face the morning

effects.log: You turn the mound a little east. The family will be lucky. It is a kindness.

choices.text: Make the grave site lucky for her line

effects.log: Her line prospers. It is good work.

choices.text: Hold her, as you held the house

effects.log: You hold her, as gently as you held the child's house. The ground holds the living and the dead the same way, and has never once told them apart.

events.text: A king wants to build a new palace on the site above you, a great one, nine courts deep. You can already feel the old weight coming back: the House, the throne, the centre of everything, on your back again.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Let him build, and do not rise to hold it up

ok.log: He builds, and the palace stands on the ground, as palaces do, and you do not lift it, and it does not sink. It never needed you to carry it. It needed you to be the ground.

fail.log: He builds, and you rise to hold it up out of old habit before you can stop yourself, and it is very heavy.

choices.text: Let him build, and bless the centre pillar

effects.log: You bless the pillar, and take the weight, as a dragon of the centre does. It is your oldest work.

choices.text: Refuse, and shake the site

effects.log: You shake the site, and the king's builders flee, and he builds somewhere else, afraid of you.

events.text: It is the eighteen days before winter, and you lie at the centre of everything, and you are not carrying any of it. Houses, fields, graves, palaces, the four directions: they rest on you, and you hold them as the ground holds, patiently, without weight. If you let go of the dragon, you will be the earth.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You settle a little deeper under the fields for one more year, and the rice grows over you, and nobody knows.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Earth

effects.log: You set down the last weight, and find you are still holding everything.

events.text: You try to be the ground, and you are still lifting. Somewhere in you a house is still on your back, and you have not set it down.
events.arc: The Yellow Dragon: The Dao of Earth

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years lying fallow under the fields, until you find the weight you are still lifting.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Yellow Dragon of the centre, and the four will bring you their cases. The centre is not small.

events.text: The jade floor of your hall goes warm under your feet, like a field at noon, and the whole Upper Realm settles, very slightly, as a house settles. Up out of the floor, without breaking a single tile, comes a yellow dragon, coiled like a hill. "You were me," it says. "I held everything. Now I am what everything stands on. Even up here."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow, and it sinks back through the floor, and for a year your hall is the steadiest place in heaven.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Earth from it

effects.log: It puts its great head down and touches your feet, and you feel the ground come up into you, patient beyond counting.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world. "Every house there should stand," it says. "Every grave should rest. I will be under them."

events.text: An old smith dies at his anvil in a village you once walked through hungry. You lie outside the forge and watch the village gather up his tongs and hammers and melt them down into a plough for his grave field, as the old custom says.
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Eat his tools before they melt them

effects.log: You eat them in the night, the hammers and the tongs and the anvil horn. They taste of a long, good life. The village has no plough for his field.

choices.text: Lie by the forge until it is cold

effects.log: You lie there until the fire goes out and the iron is a plough. The rice in your tail is warm.

choices.text: Watch the iron go back into the field

effects.log: In spring they plough his field with what was in his hands. Death is the iron going back into the field. You have been eating iron for a thousand years. You have never once watched it go home.

events.text: A soldier sleeps in a ditch below your hill, and the nightmare coming out of him is the one you have eaten a hundred times from a hundred soldiers: the face of the man he killed. You lie down to eat it, as you always have.
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Leave it: it is his

effects.log: You leave it. He wakes shouting, and goes on, and carries it.

choices.text: Eat it, as you always do

effects.log: You eat it, and he sleeps, and wakes lighter, and the rice in your tail is warmer.

choices.text: Taste it slowly before you eat it

effects.log: What he fears is not death. It is that the man he killed is still dying in him, every night, and cannot finish. Death is not the cruelty. Death that cannot end is.

events.text: Fire at the tail: it is the only death you have ever had to fear. Tonight a village child comes up the hill with a torch, out of nothing but curiosity, to see the iron beast up close, and holds the flame out towards you.
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Hide the tail

effects.log: You fold your tail under you, and the child is a little disappointed and goes home.

choices.text: Warn the child gently

effects.log: You rumble, kindly, and the child lowers the torch and sits with you, and you tell each other things.

choices.text: Let the child come near

effects.log: The torch comes close enough to warm the rice in your tail. You are not afraid. This surprises you more than anything has in a thousand years. Death is close, and it is only warm.

events.text: The swords inside you talk at night, as they always have: the old owners, in borrowed voices. Tonight one of them, a woman who died on a pass three hundred years ago, says only: "I am tired. Let me rest."
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Keep her: their voices are company

effects.log: You keep her. She goes quiet, and the others go on talking, and you are not lonely.

choices.text: Ask her what death was like

effects.log: She tells you. It was like setting down a load at the end of a long road. She wants to finish setting it down.

choices.text: Give her sword back to her grave

effects.log: You walk four hundred li to her grave on the pass and lay her sword on it, and spit out the iron you took with it. Something in you that was never asleep goes to sleep.

events.text: A monk of your maker's line, very old, lies dying in the attic of the temple where you were made from three grains of rice. He asks you, as if you were a friend: "Are you afraid of dying? You cannot, can you."
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Try to keep him alive with the heat in you

effects.log: You lie against the attic wall and pour your heat into him, and he lives a season, coughing, and asks you to stop.

choices.text: Tell him the truth: you cannot, and you are learning what it costs

effects.log: He laughs, and coughs, and holds your iron paw. "Then you will have to learn it from us," he says.

choices.text: Sit with him until he dies, and keep nothing from it

ok.log: You sit with him to the end, and do not eat the grief, and do not keep his voice. When it is over, you are lighter. Death is a rest that is given back. You have been the one thing in the world that could not rest.

fail.log: You sit with him to the end, and at the last you swallow the grief out of habit, and it sits in you like a cold blade.

events.text: On the night of the dark moon you lie on your maker's grave, a hill of rusted iron with pines in it, and you understand what you could never be killed by, and why that was the saddest thing about you. Death is not the end. It is the rest, the giving back, the iron going home to the field. If you let go of the beast, you will be it.
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: Not yet. You get up off the grave, and go and lie outside a farmhouse where a child has bad dreams, one more night.

choices.text: Become the Dao of Death

effects.log: You lie down on the grave, and for the first time in your life, you rest.

events.text: You lie down to be the rest, and the iron in you will not lie still. Somewhere in you a voice, a sword, a grief is still being kept from going home.
events.arc: The Iron-Eater: The Dao of Death

choices.text: Sit with it ten years more

effects.log: Ten more years on your maker's grave, letting things go home, until you find the one you are still keeping.

choices.text: Let it go: in this life you will not be the Dao

effects.log: You let it go. In this life you will be the Iron-Eater, and no blade will be raised against you. That, too, is an ending of a kind.

events.text: A sound like a forge at night: something enormous and rusted and very quiet comes down the jade stair, with pines growing out of its back and sword hilts worn smooth as river stones. Every weapon the immortals carry goes still in its sheath. It lies down in front of you. "You were me," it says, in a voice that has been many voices and is now one. "I learned to rest. You can too, one day."
events.arc: The Dao Beast

choices.text: Thank it, and let it go back to the sky

effects.log: You bow, and it lies there a while, resting, and then it is gone, and every blade in the Upper Realm is quieter for a year.

choices.text: Take the Dao of Death from it

effects.log: It breathes out, slow, and you understand what death is for, and you are not afraid of it any more.

choices.text: Ask it to guard your world

effects.log: It looks down at your world. "Things there should end gently," it says. "And rest. I will see to that."

events.arc: The Dao Beast
events.text: On a moonless night the sky over the Upper Realm fills with what you were: thunder in a pool, the first wind of spring, an autumn blade, water under ice, a scale with no hand, the bamboo flowering, a ribbon coming home, the moon in every cup, the fire given away, the ground beneath all houses, the iron that learned to rest. Every one of them was once you. They turn around you like the sky around the pole star.

choices.text: Bow to all of them

effects.log: You bow, once to each, and each one bows back. It takes the whole night, and the immortals who see it from their terraces never speak of it to anyone.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you, all together

effects.log: They come closer. It is like standing in all the weather of the world at once.

choices.text: Ask them only to remember you

effects.log: "We are what remembers," says the thunder, and the fire, and the ground, together. "That is all we have ever been."
